title: Eviction coordinator regression — on-call scratchpad and synthesis
content:
Summary:
During a change rolled out 2025-01-17 (runtime kernel selection tweak + eviction tuning), several hosts experienced repeated transient OOMs during sustained traffic spikes. The common surface is the eviction coordinator loop: hosts show extended eviction latencies and a rise in live-set churn, after which some processes hit memory limits and get OOM-killed. This doc is the on-call scratchpad capturing timeline, immediate mitigations, evidence, hypotheses, and follow-ups.

Impact:
- Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-5 (NVIDIA A800, multi-tenant).
- Symptoms: 5-12% request failures with 5xx on a 30m window, increased p99 latency for generation requests, host process restarts on ~3 hosts.
- Customer visible: intermittent timeouts for a subset of requests; alerting noise for batch queue saturations.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-01-17 02:10: deploy: rolling config change (dynconfig) updated eviction goal to target 12% headroom and enabled kernel selector v2.
- 2025-01-17 02:22: first SLO alerts (batch queue depth rising).
- 2025-01-17 02:45: surge in host memory usage observed on host-17, host-21.
- 2025-01-17 03:00: host-21 OOM and restarted the serving process (killed by kernel).
- 2025-01-17 03:05: oncall paged; mitigation experiment begun.
- 2025-01-17 03:20: rolled back eviction goal change on the pool and reverted kernel selector to v1 on a canary subset.
- 2025-01-17 03:40: memory growth rates decreased on rolled-back hosts; other hosts continued to show oscillations.
- 2025-01-17 08:00: follow-up alerts quieted but telemetry indicates higher-than-baseline churn across the pool for several hours.

Immediate mitigation actions taken (what worked / what didn't):
1) Scoped rollback: Reverted eviction goal tweak (12% headroom) to previous setting (20% headroom) for pool-5 — reduced eviction latency and prevented further immediate OOMs on most hosts. (effective)
2) Kernel selector rollback: Reverted kernel selector v2 -> v1 on 10% canary hosts and observed stable memory behaviour within 30m. (partially effective)
3) Increased eviction aggressiveness via dynconfig on two hot hosts as stopgap — reduced live-set by ~18% but increased CPU on eviction thread (tradeoff). (effective but costly)
4) Eviction coordinator isolated restart on two hosts (graceful): temporarily reduced thrash but resumed when traffic shifted. (temporary)
5) No restarts of full host — we avoided infra-level restarts to preserve locality and cache warmness.

Key telemetry / logs / artifacts collected:
- heap-summaries: /artifacts/heap-summaries/2025-01-17/pool5-host21-heap.txt
- eviction traces: sampled coordinator trace (10s windows) showing 3x longer scan times post-change.
- perf counters: increase in page-faults and runtime allocation rate coincident with kernel selector v2 on canaries.
- metric snapshot (pre-change vs post-change):
  - avg-eviction-latency: 12ms -> 62ms
  - kv-live-set-size: +22% on hottest tenants
  - host-memory-usage: 64% -> 89% peak on impacted hosts

Observed behaviour (notes from slog):
- Eviction coordinator scan loops appear to re-scan portions of the cache more often instead of progressing; there are repeated short sleeps and then long GC-like scanning bursts.
- When combined with continuous-batching spikes, eviction CPU contends with batching worker threads, and the host allocator reports bursts of small allocations (likely temporary metadata).
- Kernel selector v2 attempts to pick more optimized kernels for certain attention patterns; these kernels allocate a small extra scratch buffer per request which multiplied under heavy batching and increased transient resident set.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Secondary allocation growth from kernel selector v2 plus reduced eviction headroom produced momentary spike in resident set; eviction coordinator scan latency increased because it encountered more hot-churn buckets and did more per-key work. (high confidence)
2) Eviction coordinator preemption: the coordinator relies on nice scheduling; under heavier CPU due to kernel paths, it loses CPU and thus delays eviction scans, creating positive feedback. (medium confidence)
3) A regressive change in the eviction compaction logic (recent refactor) created a pathological re-scan loop for certain index boundary conditions; combined with the kernel change, it surfaced. (low->medium confidence)

Reproduction notes and quick experiments to run locally / on canary:
- Re-run load generator with continuous-batching pattern (seq length profile A) against a canary host with kernel selector v2 and eviction headroom 12% to measure step memory. Use load profile script: tools/loadgen/continuous_batch_profile_A.sh
- Turn on verbose eviction tracing (env EVIC_TRACE=1) and capture a full 5-minute trace.
- Run heap profiles (jemalloc + pprof) during spike to inspect resident allocations from new kernels (look for ident string kernel_v2_scratch).

Short-term action items (owners):
- Ana Gomez: finish synthesis and publish this scratchpad (today).
- Tomoko Saito: coordinate a full canary rollback of kernel selector v2 for all dedicated pools (in progress).
- Ravi Patel: instrument eviction coordinator with an in-band progress metric (PR draft in linked_artifacts) to detect re-scan loops (owner: Ravi, due 2025-01-24).
- Ethan Morales: correlate per-request kernel selection logs with memory allocations to quantify contribution (due 2025-01-22).

Longer-term remediation (postmortem and engineering work):
- Add eviction coordinator watchdog: if a scan takes > X ms repeatedly, escalate and temporarily raise eviction aggressiveness automatically.
- Add per-kernel scratch allocation accounting so runtime can choose more memory-conservative kernels under constrained host memory.
- Revisit default eviction headroom heuristics: consider adaptive headroom based on observed allocation variance during load spikes.
- Run regular stress tests that combine continuous-batching workload with kernel-selection experiments in CI.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does kernel selector v2 have any other transient allocations beyond the scratch buffer? (Ethan to confirm).
- Is there a measurable scheduling preemption effect causing coordinator starvation, or is it strictly allocation economics? (Tomoko to gather perf samples).
- Did any tenant-specific workload patterns (extreme prefix reuse) bias the eviction tracker into pathological behavior? (Ana to audit top-5 tenants).

After-action notes (lessons for runbook):
- When rolling out kernel or low-level runtime changes, gate them behind a combined memory-churn test that includes eviction and batching traffic patterns.
- Eviction headroom changes should be toggled conservatively and simulated for high-churn tenants.
- Provide a quick rollback playbook: (1) set headroom back to baseline, (2) disable kernel selector variant, (3) enable aggressive eviction on hot hosts, (4) watch for OOMs for 60m.

Draft runbook snippet (to lift into playbooks/eviction-runbook):
- Trigger: repeated high eviction latency OR host RSS > 85% + batch queue p99 > threshold.
- Immediate steps (SRE):
  1) Pin dynconfig eviction_headroom to 20% for affected pool.
  2) Revert kernel selector to previous stable version for the pool.
  3) Run `sudo -u runtimectl runtime evict --pool <pool> --aggressive` on top-3 noisy hosts.
  4) If >2 hosts OOM in 30m, move traffic away from pool and engage runtime oncall.
- Diagnostics to collect: eviction_trace, heap profile, kernel-selection log, top 50 tenants by live-set.

Next calendar steps:
- 2025-01-20: retro meeting with serving-runtime and applied-ml to review kernel selector rollout process. (invitees: runtime, applied-ml, eng-sre, product-hosted-api)
- 2025-01-24: PR for eviction progress metric and automated throttle (owner: Ravi).
- 2025-01-28: run combined stress job in CI with kernel selector v2 toggled.

Notes to self: keep this doc iterative — capture any new traces and paste here. We should avoid too formal language for now; this is the working oncall artifact.

Appendix (useful commands):
- Collect eviction trace: curl -s http://host:21000/debug/evictrace?duration=30s > /tmp/evictrace.txt
- Heap profile (if jemalloc): /usr/local/bin/heapdump --duration 30s --out /artifacts/heap-profile-host17.pb
  // convert with pprof: go tool pprof -http :6060 /usr/local/bin/serving-runtime /artifacts/heap-profile-host17.pb
- Force aggressive eviction: runtimectl evict --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-5 --aggressive --top 3
- Disable kernel selector for a host: sudo systemctl set-environment RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy && systemctl restart serving-runtime

End of scratchpad.
